text:
Jack Hughes ended it 3:23 into overtime with a wrist shot off a Jesper Bratt feed, and for once the result matched the play. New Jersey beat Philadelphia 3-2 at Prudential Center after outshooting the Flyers 44-25 on goal and 95-41 in total attempts. The Devils generated 4.41 expected goals to Philadelphia's 1.86, which means that if you replayed every shot, New Jersey wins about 86 percent of the time.

Philadelphia led twice on a handful of quiet chances. Rasmus Ristolainen tipped one in at 11:12 of the first, a play with just a 10 percent chance of scoring, and Travis Sanheim's slap shot early in the third carried only a 4 percent chance. Dougie Hamilton tied it late in the second, and Luke Hughes did the same at 9:44 of the third, a snap shot that came from a better look (17 percent). Every goal came at even strength, and New Jersey's power play went 0 for 4 while Philadelphia's went 0 for 1.

The gap between shot volume and score belonged to Joseph Woll. He faced 44 shots worth 4.41 expected goals and allowed three, a margin of 1.41 goals saved above expectation that earned him the third star. Jake Allen, at the other end, stopped 23 of 25 against 1.86 expected, a bit short of par. Bratt led the Devils with six shots, and Jack Hughes logged 25:48 and finished with five. The Flyers blocked 32 shots, and it still wasn't enough to hold off the Devils.
